questions.q: In this lab's scenario, what is the first thing checked after the warehouse lead reports the inventory sync flow as "stuck"?
options: The Flow Execution Log, to see whether it's genuinely failed or just correctly paused
The integration's transform script, to look for a bug
The Connection & Credential Alias, to see if it needs refreshing
The vendor's status page, before looking at anything inside ServiceNow
questions.explain: Per Lesson 17, "stuck" is ambiguous until the execution log confirms a real failure rather than a legitimate pause — so that's checked first.

questions.q: The execution record shows the REST action step's status as Error, not Requested or Pending. What does this confirm?
options: The flow has genuinely failed at a specific step, ruling out "it's just waiting on an approval"
The flow is waiting on an approval that hasn't been actioned yet
The Script Performance Profiler found a bug in the transform script
The inventory vendor's API is definitely down
questions.explain: An Error status on the current step is the signature of a genuine failure, distinct from a pending/requested approval wait.

questions.q: Why does the lab treat the matching entry in the integration's own structured gs.error() log as valuable, given the execution log already showed an error?
options: It's independent corroboration — two separate sources agreeing on the same transaction ID, status code, and timestamp is stronger evidence than either alone
It replaces the need to check the Flow Execution Log at all
It proves the problem is a bug in the flow's own configuration
Structured logs are only useful before a failure happens, not after
questions.explain: The lab explicitly treats two independent sources confirming the same 503 as stronger than a single source.

questions.q: The failed step returns HTTP 503. Per the bug-vs-external fork from Lesson 16, what does a 503 point to, as opposed to a 401 or a 429?
options: An outage — the external system itself is unavailable, rather than rate-limiting (429) or an expired credential (401)
A recursive business rule trigger inside the flow
A missing database index on the order table
A UI policy conflict on the sales order form
questions.explain: 503 Service Unavailable is the outage signature, distinct from the rate-limit (429) and expired-credential (401) signatures.

questions.q: Once the vendor's own status page confirms a matching outage, what is the correct final action in this lab?
options: Communicate the root cause clearly to the stakeholder — the platform and flow are working correctly, and resolution depends on the vendor, not a ServiceNow code change
Edit the flow's REST action configuration to work around the outage
Reassign the Connection & Credential Alias used by the action
Rewrite the transform script to retry indefinitely without logging anything
questions.explain: With the cause confirmed as external, the correct response is accurate communication, not a code change to logic that was never broken.
